displayName: Kiwiplan MES (Java 11 → Java 21 / Spring Boot 3, JUnit 5)
description: Reference Java 11 → Java 21 LTS + Spring Boot 3 IN-PLACE modernization scaffold for a Kiwiplan MES work-order slice, from a signed java spec (schemaId=java, targetStack=java-spring). Source and target are both Java, so this shows the MODERNIZED forms rather than a language translation: a verbose POJO → a record (Dimensions/WorkItem); an int status + if-else → a sealed interface + pattern-matching switch (WorkOrderState/WorkOrderStateMachine); new Date(y-1900,m-1,d)/new Integer(int) → java.time.LocalDate/Integer.valueOf (ShipmentScheduler); collect(Collectors.toList()) that is later mutated → a mutable copy of Stream.toList() (BatchPlanner, the unmodifiable-toList edge case); and multi-line concatenation → a text block (PricingReport). The framework-level upgrades — javax.* → jakarta.*, WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter → SecurityFilterChain — cannot compile offline (no Spring/jakarta in the maven-sidecar cache) and are documented @Modernization contracts (SecurityConfigContract), not stubbed. Builds OFFLINE on the sidecar's JDK 21 with real JUnit tests that verify behaviour is preserved across the upgrade. This completes the portfolio: Java is the last of the client's source languages to get a migration stack.

matches.fallback: Used for java routines being modernized to Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 (jakarta move, removed/deprecated APIs, Spring Boot 2→3, or Java 21 language adoption).

verification.sourceExecutionEquivalenceReason: Source and target are both Java, so equivalence is feasible in principle (run Java 11 vs Java 21 on the same inputs) — but it is not wired, and the framework-level upgrades can't run offline anyway. The golden score + this JUnit suite are the gates.
